name: Site Migration
description: Move a site's data from one Alvyth install to another — pick what travels, export a bundle, import it there.
long_description:
Site Migration moves the work you have already done from one Alvyth install to another. Staging to production. An agency template to a client's site. A shop rebuilt on new hosting. You choose what travels, export a single file, carry it to the second install running this same plugin, and import it there.

It is not a backup tool and does not try to be one. A backup restores over an identical schema on the same install; this merges selected data into a different install that already has content of its own. Those are different problems, and a tool claiming both does neither well.

Records find themselves on the destination by their natural key — a product by its SKU, a page by its slug, a category by its slug — never by database id, because an id means nothing outside the database that issued it. That is what makes importing the same bundle twice safe: the second run updates what it already placed rather than creating a second copy of everything.

Every module you tick is checked against its own permission, in both directions. Exporting products needs permission to view products; importing them needs permission to create them, and overwriting needs permission to update them. Being allowed to run a migration is never, on its own, permission to rewrite the catalogue.

Nothing secret rides along. Payment gateway keys, the SMTP password and the AI key are stripped from every bundle unless you explicitly opt in, and then only sealed under a passphrase you choose and carry separately from the file itself.

Large sites are handled a few thousand records at a time. A run that does not finish in one press leaves a Continue button and picks up exactly where it stopped, rather than a request that dies half-way through with a partly written database.
